overview: The Medford City Council Committee of the Whole held its fourth preliminary budget hearing for fiscal year 2027 to review departmental requests and city liabilities. The committee discussed funding for new assessing software, facilities maintenance, debt service for school projects, and rising healthcare and insurance costs.

items.title: 26061: Annual Budget Process for Fiscal 27 Preliminary Budget Meeting Number 4
items.summary: The committee opened the meeting to review various city department budgets and kept the matter in committee following the discussion.

items.title: Assessing Department Budget Review
items.summary: Chief Assessor Jared Yagjian discussed revaluation cycles and proposed purchasing aerial detection software to identify unpermitted property growth. The department is also focusing on increased outreach for veteran and senior tax exemptions.

items.title: Facilities Department Budget Review
items.summary: Director David McIntyre presented plans to shift toward preventative maintenance and discussed a future redesign of the City Council chambers to accommodate more members. The budget reflects an 8% increase in utility costs and rising repair expenses.

items.title: Bonds and Interest (Debt Service) Budget Review
items.summary: CFO Bob Dickinson reported on interest payments for the $225.7 million school HVAC borrowing and noted that city debt currently accounts for approximately 5% of the general fund.

items.title: Pension Budget Review
items.summary: CFO Dickinson confirmed the city remains on track to fully fund pension obligations by 2033 and discussed long-term strategies for addressing OPEB liabilities related to retiree health insurance.

items.title: Workers' Compensation Budget Review
items.summary: The committee reviewed a budget increase intended to cover higher medical evaluation costs and to formally budget for settlement payments. HR Director Lisa Crowley noted an increase in medical and physical therapy costs for injured employees.

items.title: Insurance Budget Review
items.summary: Officials discussed a 9% increase in GIC health insurance premiums and the impact of school department payroll growth on city Medicare obligations. CFO Dickinson clarified that general liability insurance covers property and injury claims but not labor disputes or arbitrations.
